 Wake Forest built a 42-0 first-half lead in Dallas after three College GameDay panelists picked SMU, prompting a playful mea culpa and a nod to Jake Dickert. Matt De Lima | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source Pat McAfee, right, talks to Kirk Herbstreit on the set of ESPN College GameDay | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect In this story:
 Wake Forest Demon Deacons SMU Mustangs ESPN analysts Kirk Herbstreit and Pat McAfee owned their College GameDay miss on Saturday, issuing a playful apology to Wake Forest as the Demon Deacons stormed out to a 42-0 first-half lead at SMU in Dallas.
--> ESPN analysts Kirk Herbstreit and Pat McAfee owned their College GameDay miss on Saturday, issuing a playful apology to Wake Forest as the Demon Deacons stormed out to a 42-0 first-half lead at SMU in Dallas.
 Herbstreit posted a video to X with McAfee at his side, writing that the pair wanted to “apologize from the bottom of our hearts for picking against” Wake Forest. “We thought SMU at home had a chance and boy, were we wrong,” Herbstreit wrote. “These boys are for real!”

— Kirk Herbstreit (@KirkHerbstreit) November 14, 2026 The clip played out like two friends caught on the wrong side of a blowout and trying to laugh their way out of it. McAfee opened by crediting Wake Forest coach Jake Dickert, who appeared on the show that morning. “He was so good on the show today,” McAfee said. “We should have known. That’s on us.”
--> The clip played out like two friends caught on the wrong side of a blowout and trying to laugh their way out of it. McAfee opened by crediting Wake Forest coach Jake Dickert, who appeared on the show that morning. “He was so good on the show today,” McAfee said. “We should have known. That’s on us.”
 Herbstreit then explained the thinking behind the pick. “I thought, you know, they’re on the road,” the former Ohio State quarterback said. “SMU looked so good last week. I thought maybe they’re in a spot to upset Wake. Boy, were we wrong.”
--> Herbstreit then explained the thinking behind the pick. “I thought, you know, they’re on the road,” the former Ohio State quarterback said. “SMU looked so good last week. I thought maybe they’re in a spot to upset Wake. Boy, were we wrong.”
 McAfee had a quick answer for that logic. “SMU looked good last week. You know who else did? Wake,” he said. “Wake has looked good every week.”
--> McAfee had a quick answer for that logic. “SMU looked good last week. You know who else did? Wake,” he said. “Wake has looked good every week.”
 The pair then brought in Herbstreit’s golden retriever, Peter , with McAfee joking that the dog “picked Wake. He knew.” They wrapped up with praise for Dickert, as McAfee said “Love Jake” and Herbstreit added, “Jake’s the man. Go Deacs.”

 Wake Forest Demon Deacons WR Carlos Hernandez (8), TE Will Loerzel (85) and WR Antonio Meeks celebrate | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The GameDay desk split on the matchup Saturday morning. Desmond Howard and Nick Saban took Wake Forest, while Herbstreit, McAfee and guest picker Ian Johnson sided with the Mustangs.
--> The GameDay desk split on the matchup Saturday morning. Desmond Howard and Nick Saban took Wake Forest, while Herbstreit, McAfee and guest picker Ian Johnson sided with the Mustangs.
 The SMU pick made some sense on paper. The Mustangs entered 7-2 after a 51-28 win over Virginia Tech, and SMU coach Rhett Lashlee had gone 15-2 in November games since 2022.
--> The SMU pick made some sense on paper. The Mustangs entered 7-2 after a 51-28 win over Virginia Tech, and SMU coach Rhett Lashlee had gone 15-2 in November games since 2022.
 But none of that showed up on homecoming and Senior Day at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Ty Clark III opened the scoring on a 27-yard run, Gio Lopez hit Carlos Hernandez for a 44-yard touchdown and the Wake Forest quarterback ran for two more scores before halftime. SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings completed 7 of 12 passes for 40 yards with an interception in the first half.
